subject.title: fix(agents): bound finished bash process session retention

question: Should completed bash process records be allowed to expire before the configured TTL when the 50-session or 2,000,000-character budget is exceeded?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but it intentionally shortens an existing observable retention window to bound gateway memory, which requires owner intent rather than automated judgment.

options.title: Accept bounded eviction
options.body: Keep the proposed budgets and treat the configured TTL as a maximum duration rather than a guaranteed poll/log window under burst load.

options.title: Revise the retention contract
options.body: Choose different budgets or another bounded design that preserves a longer delayed-poll window and update proof accordingly.

options.title: Defer this approach
options.body: Leave the linked issue open if maintainers are unwilling to shorten completed-record availability before TTL.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded eviction
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed budgets and treat the configured TTL as a maximum duration rather than a guaranteed poll/log window under burst load.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history in the same process registry and tests is the best available ownership signal for this choice.
